nodes.title: SG-1 · Bootstrap StoryForge monorepo modules
nodes.body:
Context: Tip product tree is documentation-only (`README.md` = `hello Worldseed`); no application modules exist and the repo has no product top-level folders yet.
Desired behavior: Repository gains StoryForge Phase-1 bootstrap as root-level module files — frontend (React/TypeScript/Vite), backend+worker (one Go module with Chi + YAML), game runtime/content files, YAML configs, example env files, and GitOps world/round YAML — because new nested top-level dirs cannot be planned until those folders exist on disk.
Expected result: Root module manifests and example configs are present; unit tests for config loading and module wiring pass with filesystem and external I/O mocked.
Why: Unlocks later playable game, GitOps rounds, API, and Local Worker work once the empty-repo bootstrap lands.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a clean clone of the repository tip, when bootstrap work for SG-1 is complete, then root-level StoryForge module files exist: `package.json`, `go.mod`, game runtime/content sources, GitOps YAML (`world.yaml`, `current-release.yaml`, `round.yaml`), and updated `README.md`.
- Given the bootstrapped modules, when config-loading and module-wiring unit tests run with filesystem and external I/O mocked, then those unit tests pass.
- Given example env and YAML config files, when an engineer opens the repo, then required keys are documented via `.env.example` and `*.example.yaml` without requiring live services.


## Scope
- In scope: Scaffold frontend React/TypeScript/Vite files at repo root
- In scope: Scaffold Go Chi backend and worker in one root Go module with YAML config loading
- In scope: Scaffold game runtime vs content as separate root source/content files
- In scope: Create GitOps world/round YAML and root example env
- In scope: Unit tests for config loading and module wiring with mocked FS/I/O
- Out of scope: Playable Boy's Room gameplay and 80/20 UI beyond stubs
- Out of scope: REST contribution/admin APIs beyond minimal backend wiring
- Out of scope: Round lifecycle state machine beyond seed YAML
- Out of scope: Local Worker AI pipeline, Claude Code CLI, release publishing
- Out of scope: Databases, message queues, Firebase, or microservices
- Out of scope: Creating nested top-level folders that do not yet exist on disk
- Preserve: .gitignore Devion ignore entries
- Preserve: No database, queue, or Firebase introduction
- Preserve: Git as intended durable store for worlds/rounds data


## Technical constraints
- Mandatory stack: frontend React+TypeScript+Vite; backend Go+Chi; worker Go
- Mandatory: YAML configuration for Go services; no PostgreSQL/MongoDB/MySQL/Redis
- Mandatory: separate game runtime source from declarative content; separate GitOps YAML from game content files
- Mandatory (empty tip): Act code_paths and step files must be repository-root files until product top-level directories exist
- Suggestion: keep Phase-1 entrypoints minimal (health/stub) so later phases can extend


## Definition of done
- All SG-1 requirements have linked Act and Verify units completed
- Config/wiring unit tests for each module slice pass with mocked I/O
- Evidence ticket can cite those Verify results


## Non-functional requirements
- Module layout must remain simple and navigable for future coding agents
- Secrets must not be committed; only example env/config files
- Phase-1 files stay at repository root until top-level module folders exist on disk for later reorganizations


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Frontend React/TypeScript/Vite module scaffold
nodes.body:
Context: No `package.json` or Vite app exists at tip.
Desired behavior: Root gains a Vite + React + TypeScript app with `loadFrontendConfig` reading `VITE_API_BASE_URL` and `VITE_APP_NAME`, plus `.env.example` documenting those keys.
Expected result: Engineers can run the StoryForge web app from the repo root; config resolves defaults when env keys are absent.
Why: Establishes the player/admin UI host for later phases.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the repository after this requirement, when listing the repo root, then `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, and `main.tsx` exist.
- Given `loadFrontendConfig` with empty env, when called, then it returns `apiBaseUrl` default `http://localhost:8080` and `appName` default `StoryForge`.
- Given root `.env.example`, when opened, then it documents `VITE_API_BASE_URL` and `VITE_APP_NAME`.


## Scope
- In scope: Vite React TS scaffold at repository root
- In scope: Typed frontend config loader and `.env.example`
- In scope: Minimal App stub rendering the StoryForge name from config
- Out of scope: 80/20 gameplay UI
- Out of scope: Contribution submission UI
- Out of scope: Admin screens
- Out of scope: Calling live backend APIs
- Preserve: No hardcoded production secrets in source


## Technical constraints
- Mandatory: React, TypeScript, Vite
- Mandatory: config via Vite VITE_* env vars with example file
- Mandatory: new files at repository root only (no frontend/ folder yet)


## Dependencies
- INT-SG1


## Definition of done
- Frontend module files exist as specified
- Linked Act and Verify units complete


## Non-functional requirements
- TypeScript strictness enabled in tsconfig


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Backend Go/Chi module with YAML config
nodes.body:
Context: No Go modules exist at tip.
Desired behavior: Root Go module with Chi router wiring and YAML config loaded through `fs.FS` (not hard-wired only to live disk in the load function used by tests).
Expected result: `go.mod`, `main.go`, `config.go`, `router.go`, and `config.example.yaml` exist; config load returns typed server listen address and git repo path fields.
Why: Backend is the REST/GitOps API host for later phases; Phase-1 only needs scaffold + config wiring.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the repository after this requirement, when inspecting the repo root, then `go.mod`, `main.go`, `config.go`, `router.go`, and `config.example.yaml` exist.
- Given a YAML document with `server.addr: ":8080"` and `git.repo_path: "."`, when `LoadFS` reads it via `fs.FS`, then the returned Config has Addr `":8080"` and RepoPath `"."`.
- Given `NewRouter`, when constructed, then it registers GET `/healthz` returning HTTP 200 body `ok`.


## Scope
- In scope: Go module scaffold with Chi at repo root
- In scope: YAML config struct + LoadFS
- In scope: Minimal Chi router with /healthz
- In scope: Example YAML config file
- Out of scope: Player/contribution/admin API handlers
- Out of scope: Real Git commit operations
- Out of scope: Authentication
- Out of scope: Nested backend/ directory tree
- Preserve: No database driver or ORM introduction


## Technical constraints
- Mandatory: Go, Chi HTTP router, YAML configuration
- Mandatory: config loading testable via fs.FS / io.Reader without network I/O
- Mandatory: new Go files at repository root only


## Dependencies
- INT-SG1


## Definition of done
- Backend module and example config exist
- Linked Act and Verify units complete


## Non-functional requirements
- Keep dependencies minimal (Chi + YAML decoder only for Phase-1)


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Game module runtime separated from content
nodes.body:
Context: No game sources exist.
Desired behavior: Separate runtime (`runtime.ts`) from content (`world-content.yaml`, `bedroom.yaml`), with a content loader that parses world YAML from an injected string source.
Expected result: Runtime exports a minimal `createRuntime` stub; content includes the-boys-room world YAML; loader returns typed world id/title without touching network.
Why: Coding agents must extend content without rewriting engine layout.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the repository after this requirement, when inspecting the root, then `runtime.ts` and `world-content.yaml` exist as separate runtime vs content files.
- Given `world-content.yaml` text with `id: the-boys-room` and `title: The Boy's Room`, when `loadWorldFromYaml` parses it, then it returns matching `id` and `title`.
- Given root `package.json`, when opened, then it names the package and includes TypeScript tooling without embedding world prose into `runtime.ts`.


## Scope
- In scope: runtime.ts engine stub
- In scope: world-content.yaml and bedroom.yaml declarative content
- In scope: YAML world loader function
- In scope: yaml dependency on root package.json
- Out of scope: Clickable objects, dialogue/choice engines, inventory
- Out of scope: Pixel art assets
- Out of scope: React 80/20 UI
- Out of scope: Nested game/ directory tree
- Preserve: Runtime vs content file separation


## Technical constraints
- Mandatory: declarative YAML content in world-content.yaml / bedroom.yaml
- Mandatory: reusable runtime in runtime.ts
- Suggestion: TypeScript for game module to align with HTML5 delivery


## Dependencies
- INT-SG1


## Definition of done
- Game runtime/content files exist
- Linked Act and Verify units complete


## Non-functional requirements
- Loader must report parse errors for invalid YAML rather than silently succeeding


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Local Worker Go module with YAML config
nodes.body:
Context: No worker sources exist.
Desired behavior: Root Go module loads worker YAML config (repo path, worktree dir, agent command, execution timeout) via `fs.FS`, with example config and a stub path that loads config then exits successfully when given a path.
Expected result: Worker can be configured without live Claude CLI or network in Phase-1.
Why: Isolates Local Worker concerns for later pipeline phases.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the repository after this requirement, when inspecting the root, then `worker_config.go`, `worker.go`, and `worker.config.example.yaml` exist alongside `go.mod`.
- Given YAML with `repo_path: "."`, `worktree_dir: ".worktrees"`, `agent.command: "claude"`, and `execution.timeout_seconds: 3600`, when `LoadWorkerFS` reads it, then those fields populate the WorkerConfig struct.
- Given the example worker config file, when opened, then it includes keys for repo_path, worktree_dir, agent.command, and execution.timeout_seconds.


## Scope
- In scope: Worker YAML config load via fs.FS
- In scope: Example worker YAML config
- In scope: Stub worker entry that loads config
- Out of scope: Round polling, analysis, Claude Code invocation, publish pipeline
- Out of scope: Separate worker/ Go module directory
- Preserve: No secrets committed — example config only


## Technical constraints
- Mandatory: Go worker code in the root Go module
- Mandatory: YAML configuration; filesystem-based config suitable for later lock/execution state


## Dependencies
- INT-SG1


## Definition of done
- Worker config and stub exist in root Go module
- Linked Act and Verify units complete

nodes.title: REQ · Worlds GitOps paths and example env files
nodes.body:
Context: Tip has no GitOps world/round YAML or shared example env for the monorepo.
Desired behavior: Create root GitOps seed files (`world.yaml`, `current-release.yaml`, `round.yaml` for ROUND-0000001), root `.env.example`, update `README.md` to describe StoryForge modules, and add `layout.go` ValidateLayout over `fs.FS`.
Expected result: Required GitOps paths validate via unit test using an in-memory FS mirror; example env documents backend/worker/frontend pointers.
Why: Rounds/releases must live as Git-tracked YAML separate from game engine content files.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the repository after this requirement, when inspecting the root, then `world.yaml`, `current-release.yaml`, and `round.yaml` exist.
- Given `round.yaml`, when read, then it records `id: ROUND-0000001`, `number: 1`, `status: OPEN`, `duration_hours: 24`, `max_contributions_per_player: 5`, and `base_release: "1.0.0"`.
- Given `ValidateLayout(fs.FS)`, when the FS contains the required GitOps paths, then it returns nil; when a required path is missing, then it returns an error naming the missing path.
- Given root `.env.example`, when opened, then it documents at least `VITE_API_BASE_URL`, backend config path hint, and worker config path hint without real secrets.


## Scope
- In scope: GitOps seed YAML at repo root
- In scope: Root .env.example
- In scope: README StoryForge module map
- In scope: layout.go ValidateLayout
- Out of scope: Contribution markdown commits
- Out of scope: Round open/close services
- Out of scope: Nested worlds/ directory tree
- Preserve: Separation of GitOps YAML from game content YAML
- Preserve: .gitignore Devion ignore rules


## Technical constraints
- Mandatory: Git-tracked YAML for world/round/release metadata
- Mandatory: layout validation testable with mocked fs.FS
- Mandatory: ROUND-0000001 seed matches OPEN / 24h / max 5 / base 1.0.0


## Dependencies
- INT-SG1
- REQ-BE


## Definition of done
- GitOps YAML and examples exist
- Layout validator covered by Verify
- Linked Act and Verify units complete


## Non-functional requirements
- Do not commit noisy logs or build artifacts as source-of-truth


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Create package.json name storyforge, private true, type module, scripts dev=vite, build=tsc -b && vite build, preview=vite preview; dependencies react and react-dom ^19; devDependencies typescript ^5.6, vite ^6, @vitejs/plugin-react ^4, @types/react, @types/react-dom.
steps.expected: package.json exists with Vite React scripts and dependencies.

steps.action: Create solution-style tsconfig referencing tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json.
steps.expected: tsconfig.json references app and node configs.

steps.action: Create app tsconfig with strict true, jsx react-jsx, module ESNext, moduleResolution bundler, include main.tsx App.tsx config.ts vite-env.d.ts.
steps.code:
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "useDefineForClassFields": true,
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "moduleDetection": "force",
    "noEmit": true,
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true
  },
  "include": ["main.tsx", "App.tsx", "config.ts", "vite-env.d.ts"]
}
steps.expected: tsconfig.app.json enables strict TypeScript for app entry files.

steps.action: Create node tsconfig including vite.config.ts only.
steps.code:
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2023"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "moduleDetection": "force",
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true
  },
  "include": ["vite.config.ts"]
}
steps.expected: tsconfig.node.json covers vite.config.ts.

steps.action: Create Vite config exporting default defineConfig with plugins: [react()] from @vitejs/plugin-react.
steps.expected: vite.config.ts enables the React plugin.

steps.action: Create index.html with root div#root and script type=module src=/main.tsx.
steps.expected: index.html mounts the React entry at /main.tsx.
